title: Queued holdback preemptor with KV segmentation and soft-fairness
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Continuous batching improves GPU utilization by aggregating tokens across concurrent requests, but long-running or very large requests and aggressive KV cache residency can starve latency-sensitive traffic. Existing preemption strategies are either too heavy-handed (hard interrupts causing cache churn) or too timid (latency SLO violations for small queries).

Proposal summary: Implement a queued holdback preemptor that combines: 1) a per-queue holdback quota to reserve GPU memory and KV cache slabs for low-latency traffic; 2) KV segmentation (hot, warm, cold slabs) with soft eviction signals to reduce cold-churn; and 3) a soft-fairness scheduler that uses time-slice yields and graceful preemption windows to satisfy SLOs while maximizing throughput.

Key ideas/novelty:
- Holdback quotas: instead of instantaneous global preemption, each latency-sensitive queue gets a small reserved token budget (holdback) that guarantees admission during brief bursts without evicting large KV state.
- KV segmentation: split KV cache into hot/warm/cold segments per model-version and maintain per-queue allocation counters. Cold segment evictions are aggressive; hot segment evictions require soft-preempt coordination to avoid k-v warmup storms.
- Soft preemption semantics: preemption happens in two phases — a yield request (runtime yields CPU/GPU slice and marks request as preemptible) and a hard interrupt after a grace window. Yielding allows the serving runtime to flush interim tokens from batches and avoid orphaned KV pointers.
- Fairness algorithm: weighted deficit round robin (W-DRR) across tenant groups with a fairness weight derived from SLA tier + recent SLO breach profile. Short requests (<100ms expected) get preferential deficit adjustment to keep tails low.
- Memory-aware admission: admission controller consults a compact GPU memory estimator (includes KV slab reservations) and rejects or defers large requests if they would push expected peak beyond configurable headroom.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- p99 latency for latency-sensitive queues decreases by >=15% under mixed load compared to baseline preemptor.
- End-to-end throughput remains within -5% of baseline for steady-state workloads.
- KV cache hit rate for hot segment remains within 3% of baseline; cold churn reduced by >30%.
- Preemption hard-interrupt rate below 5% of all preemption events; majority should be yield-based.
- No increase in GPU OOM incidents in canary cluster.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype holdback quota and simple admission gate in runtime (feature flag).
2) Add KV segmentation metadata and soft-eviction API (separate flag).
3) Implement W-DRR scheduler with yield-first semantic and grace window (configurable 100-500ms).
4) Integrate memory estimator into admission and add metrics/exposed traces.
5) Run canary A/B: baseline vs holdback+segmentation on two identical dedicated pools for 72h.
6) Iterate on parameters and roll out to more clusters with gradual traffic ramp.

Testing & validation:
- Synthetic mix: 70% short chat (<=150 tokens), 20% medium (<=800 tokens), 10% long (>2k tokens).
- Run 24/72h perf jobs capturing p50/p95/p99, throughput, KV hit rates, preemptions (yield vs hard), GPU memory headroom, and fragmentation.
- Chaos tests: inject sudden large-request surge and observe eviction patterns and SLO impacts.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged canary in runtime-1.20 image on a single dedicated pool (canary group).
- If canary passes acceptance (metrics above) for 72h, enable on 10% of traffic across regions with monitoring alarms.
- Full rollout gated by post-rollout SLO metrics and sign-off from platform reliability.

Open risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: KV warmup storms when cold slabs promoted rapidly after preemption. Mitigation: throttle promotions with token-bucket and prefer warm-prefetch on predicted short request patterns.
- Risk: underestimated GPU memory footprint leads to OOMs. Mitigation: conservative headroom defaults and immediate auto-fallback to baseline preemptor on OOM detection.
- Risk: Complexity of W-DRR tuning across tenants. Mitigation: start with simple per-tier weight mapping and expose admin tuning in Console.

Documentation & observability:
- New metrics: kv_segment_hit_rate_{hot,warm,cold}, preemption_events_{yield,hard}, holdback_utilization, admission_deferrals, gpu_memory_estimate, fairness_deficit_queue_length.
- Traces: preemption_decision_trace with decision path and memory snapshot.
- Runbook: add "holdback preemptor" section with fallback steps and how to revert feature flag.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the control-plane/algorithmic changes and light runtime hooks. Deeper KV storage compaction optimizations will be a follow-up (separate ticket).
